solution: Reliability: if one computer or its cable fails only that device is affected (star); the partial mesh gives alternative paths between buildings, so a failed central switch or link does not isolate a building, although failure of a building switch still disconnects that building. Transmission speed: each device has a dedicated link to its switch, and the extra mesh links share inter-building traffic, so congestion on the central links is reduced. Scalability: new computers are added by connecting them to a building switch, and a new building can be added as another star connected to the core. Data collisions: switches send frames only to the destination port and each link is dedicated (full duplex), so collisions are effectively avoided. Cost: more switches, cabling and extra mesh links make it more expensive to install and manage than a single star.

marking_points.criterion: Reliability: single device/cable failure is isolated, and mesh links provide alternative paths between buildings (or building switch remains a single point of failure).
Transmission speed: dedicated links to switches and multiple inter-building paths reduce congestion.
Scalability: devices/buildings can be added by connecting to a switch / adding another star.
Data collisions: switched dedicated (full-duplex) links mean collisions are effectively avoided.
Cost: additional switches and redundant mesh cabling increase installation and maintenance cost.

acceptable_alternatives: Each factor must be applied to the hybrid campus design; generic definitions alone score at most 2.
partial_credit_notes: Award each independent point once, up to 5 marks. Accept equivalent correct wording or valid alternative code. Do not double-credit one idea.

verification.technical: Manual author check of every criterion against the exact statement and all guidance paragraphs; no executable component.
verification.scope: Small-office application is assessed separately in O-C3-A-007. Bus/ring topologies are not part of the 2027 guidance and are not assessed.
